title: Move from our UDF to MVVM
description:
Our current screen architecture no longer works for us. Main problems:

  • Complex — too many layers and boilerplate per screen: up to 6–7 (interactor, presenter, model mapper, view-model mapper, view-model provider, view controller, view).
  • Over-abstract — everything is hidden behind protocols; you never know what you’re working with.
  • Poor fit for SwiftUI — hard to manage state and refresh screens.
  • Hard to test — a pile of mocks per layer; hours to spin up DI.
  • Fragile — multiple states can diverge; constant threading issues.

We’re replacing it with MVVM: a screen is a view model and a view.

  • Simple — two layers instead of six or seven.
  • Familiar — the pattern most iOS engineers already know, so newcomers are productive from day one.
  • Great for SwiftUI — an observable view model drives the view directly.
  • Easy to test — dependencies come through Swift Dependencies, no per-layer mocks.
